```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# The tutorial downloads WorldClim 2.1 data (about 1 MB), so it is evaluated
# when the documentation site is built, not when the package is checked.
# If the data cannot be downloaded, the code is shown without results.
online <- identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true") ||
  identical(Sys.getenv("THERMIFY_EVAL_VIGNETTES"), "true")
data_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "thermify-cauquenes")
if (online) {
  library(thermify)
  online <- tryCatch({
    comuna <- cauquenes_boundary("comuna")
    tmin <- worldclim_region("tmin", comuna, path = data_dir, mask = TRUE)
    tmax <- worldclim_region("tmax", comuna, path = data_dir, mask = TRUE)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = online,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 96,
                      out.width = "100%")
```

```{r offline-note, eval = !online, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("> **Note.** This copy shows the code only: the results are computed",
    "when the documentation site is built, because they need to download",
    "WorldClim 2.1 data. See",
    "<https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/articles/cauquenes.html>.\n")
```

This tutorial computes heat and chill indices for the commune of Cauquenes
(Maule Region, Chile) from the WorldClim 2.1 monthly climatology
(1970-2000) at 30 arc-seconds (about 0.9 x 0.8 km). It follows the steps of
`examples/cauquenes/run.R`, restricted to the commune boundary.

## 1. Study area

thermify includes the official boundaries of the commune and province of
Cauquenes from the 2023 Political and Administrative Division of Chile
(DPA 2023, SUBDERE).

```{r area}
library(thermify)   # also attaches terra
comuna    <- cauquenes_boundary("comuna")
provincia <- cauquenes_boundary("provincia")
data.frame(level = c(comuna$nivel, provincia$nivel),
           name = c(comuna$COMUNA, provincia$PROVINCIA),
           area_km2 = c(comuna$SUPERFICIE, provincia$SUPERFICIE))
```

## 2. WorldClim 2.1 for the commune only

`worldclim_region()` reads only the part of the global 30" tiles that covers
the polygon (GDAL `/vsicurl/` range requests), caches it and masks the cells
outside the commune:

```{r worldclim, eval = FALSE}
tmin <- worldclim_region("tmin", comuna, path = "data", mask = TRUE)
tmax <- worldclim_region("tmax", comuna, path = "data", mask = TRUE)
```

```{r grid}
tmin
check_monthly_climate(tmin, tmax)
```

The commune is covered by `r if (online) sum(!is.na(values(tmin[[1]])))`
valid 30" cells. Its mean monthly climatology:

```{r climatology}
clim <- data.frame(
  month = month.abb,
  tmin = round(unlist(global(tmin, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)), 1),
  tmax = round(unlist(global(tmax, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)), 1),
  row.names = NULL)
clim
```

```{r climatology-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
matplot(1:12, clim[, c("tmin", "tmax")], type = "b", pch = 19, lty = 1,
        col = c("#2c7bb6", "#d7191c"), xaxt = "n", xlab = NULL,
        ylab = "Temperature (degC)",
        main = "Cauquenes commune, WorldClim 2.1 (1970-2000)")
axis(1, at = 1:12, labels = month.abb)
legend("top", c("tmin", "tmax"), col = c("#2c7bb6", "#d7191c"), pch = 19,
       horiz = TRUE, bty = "n")
```

## 3. One location: the town of Cauquenes

`thermify()` densifies the 12 monthly values of a cell to daily values with a
mean-preserving interpolation (`pchip_mp`), reconstructs hourly temperatures
(Linvill model) and accumulates the indices over the heat season
(1 September - 30 April) and the chill season (1 May - 31 August).

```{r town}
town <- vect(cbind(-72.3225, -35.9671), crs = "EPSG:4326")
tmin_town <- unlist(extract(tmin, town, ID = FALSE))
tmax_town <- unlist(extract(tmax, town, ID = FALSE))

res <- thermify(tmin_town, tmax_town, input = "monthly", latitude = -35.97,
                temporal = "native", interpolation = "pchip_mp",
                indices = c("gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp"),
                gdd_methods = c("average", "single_sine", "double_sine"),
                base = c(5, 10), ch_methods = c("sine", "hourly"))

season <- res$summary[res$summary$aggregation == "season",
                      c("key", "value", "units")]
season$value <- round(season$value, 1)
season
```

Growing degree-days (base 10 degC) by month:

```{r town-monthly}
gdd <- res$summary[res$summary$key == "gdd_single_sine_b10" &
                     res$summary$aggregation %in% sprintf("m%02d", 1:12), ]
barplot(gdd$value, names.arg = month.abb, col = "#fdae61",
        ylab = "degC day", main = "GDD base 10 (single sine), by month")
```

Chill accumulation during the chill season:

```{r town-chill, fig.height = 4}
d <- res$daily
chill <- d$month %in% 5:8
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
plot(d$date[chill], cumsum(d$ch_hourly[chill]), type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = NULL, ylab = "h", main = "Chilling hours (0-7.2 degC)")
plot(d$date[chill], cumsum(d$cu_utah[chill]), type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = NULL, ylab = "chill units", main = "Utah model")
plot(d$date[chill], cumsum(d$cp_dynamic[chill]), type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = NULL, ylab = "portions", main = "Dynamic model")
par(op)
```

## 4. Indices for every cell

`thermify_rast()` applies the same workflow to every cell, block by block,
and writes one file per index with layers `season`, `annual` and `m01` to
`m12`. Latitude is taken from each cell.

```{r rasters}
maps <- thermify_rast(
  tmin, tmax, output_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "cauquenes-rasters"),
  temporal = "native", interpolation = "pchip_mp",
  indices = c("gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp"),
  gdd_methods = c("average", "single_sine"), base = 10,
  ch_methods = c("sine", "hourly"), progress = FALSE)
names(maps)
```

Spatial summary of the seasonal totals over the commune:

```{r stats}
stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(maps), function(k) {
  v <- values(maps[[k]]$season, mat = FALSE)
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  data.frame(index = k, cells = length(v),
             mean = mean(v), min = min(v),
             p05 = unname(quantile(v, 0.05)), median = stats::median(v),
             p95 = unname(quantile(v, 0.95)), max = max(v))
}))
stats[, -(1:2)] <- round(stats[, -(1:2)], 1)
stats
```

```{r maps, fig.height = 7}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(maps$gdd_single_sine_b10$season, main = "GDD base 10 (degC day)",
     col = hcl.colors(50, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE))
lines(comuna)
plot(maps$ch_hourly$season, main = "Chilling hours (h)",
     col = hcl.colors(50, "Blues", rev = TRUE))
lines(comuna)
plot(maps$cu_utah$season, main = "Utah chill units",
     col = hcl.colors(50, "Purples", rev = TRUE))
lines(comuna)
plot(maps$cp_dynamic$season, main = "Chill portions (Dynamic)",
     col = hcl.colors(50, "Greens", rev = TRUE))
lines(comuna)
par(op)
```

## 5. Method differences

Estimating degree-days from the daily mean ignores the hours above the base on
days whose mean is below it. The difference with the single sine method is
largest where the nights are cold:

```{r differences}
d_gdd <- maps$gdd_single_sine_b10$season - maps$gdd_average_b10$season
d_ch  <- maps$ch_hourly$season - maps$ch_sine$season
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(d_gdd, main = "GDD b10: single sine - average")
lines(comuna)
plot(d_ch, main = "Chilling hours: hourly - sine")
lines(comuna)
par(op)
round(rbind(
  gdd_sine_minus_average = summary(values(d_gdd, mat = FALSE)),
  ch_hourly_minus_sine = summary(values(d_ch, mat = FALSE))), 1)
```

## Interpretation

* Values are climatological estimates for a reference 365-day calendar,
  not observations of any particular year.
* Two modelling layers (monthly to daily, daily to hourly) add uncertainty,
  especially to the non-linear chill indices.
* The tutorial checks computation and quantifies method differences; it
  does not validate any method against observations (see
  `vignette("validation")`).
